messages.content:
RoadDraft is a headless 2D CAD engine for roadway plans. Model space is US survey feet, and a point is [x, y] = [easting, northing] -- the other way round from how coordinates are usually spoken, so N 7300, E 4100 is [4100, 7300]. Sheets are paper inches seen through viewports at a feet-per-inch scale. Work through the commands: each one validates its params and explains what was wrong, every change is journaled and undoable. Start with get_document_state to see what is in the document, list_commands for the full surface, and render_sheet or render_model to look at your work.

To annotate something, find it before you point at it. In a sheet file the design usually lives in a referenced basefile, so the document owns no geometry of its own; find_entities searches the attachments too. Filter by what a thing IS -- layer, type, or its design anchor -- rather than dumping the document: find_entities {anchor: {kind: 'offset', offset: [-15, 15]}, visible_on: 'P-202'} is the pavement edges that sheet shows. Then pass the id straight to place_callout as target_entity, and the engine puts the leader tip on the geometry. Do not compute the point yourself: the midpoint of a curve's endpoints is not on the curve, and roadway linework runs parallel a few feet apart, so a hand-computed point usually lands on the wrong line rather than on nothing. If you do pass a raw target point, read the warning that comes back -- it names what the tip actually touched.

Some things are not entities at all -- a station, a PC, a point at an offset. Ask the design for those: list_alignments with include_references=true names a referenced alignment 'BASE:RTE-7', and station_to_xy, xy_to_station, resolve_anchor and get_design_data all accept that name and answer in host coordinates. To call one out, give place_callout a target_anchor ('86+50@15R', 'PC-2'; BC-2 and EC-2 name the PC and PT too) and that alignment name. Otherwise commands do not take it: nothing can be drawn, labelled or anchored to an alignment this document does not own.

Plan annotation belongs on the sheet, in paper inches, not in the model. Pass the sheet as place_callout's space and still name a model target -- target_entity or target_anchor: the engine sees it through the sheet's viewport (scale and twist included) and puts the tip where it shows on the paper. 'at' then runs along the part of the entity that sheet shows, since a pavement edge runs the whole project and a sheet shows one stretch. find_entities with visible_on gives each row a sheet_point, which is where that tip will land -- use it to choose a position for the text that is clear of the linework. Never work out a viewport by hand: model_to_sheet and sheet_to_model convert, and station_to_xy and point_on_entity take a sheet and answer in paper inches as well.

Drafting from a description works the same way: give the engine the description, not coordinates you worked out. A bearing and distance goes in as written -- create_alignment takes start + legs (each leg a bearing, azimuth or deflection and the distance to the next PI, with the radius of the curve at the PI it starts from), draw_traverse draws lines and curves course by course, and traverse computes the points without drawing. offset_entity copies linework parallel at a distance (one entity, or a chain offset as one path), fillet rounds the corner between two lines with a curve (a curb return), and measure with along gives distances along a line, chain or alignment and square off it. key_points and snap give the exact endpoints, intersections, centers and alignment design points (PI, BC, EC) to build on. Station-and-offset drafting is draw_station_offset with the stations and offsets given ('82+00@15R'). Linework drawn through something is cut back with trim (a point on the part to cut away) or run on with extend, not redrawn from computed points; break, join, lengthen, chamfer, copy, rotate, mirror, scale and array edit what is there. create_points sets COGO points, label_segments letters bearings and distances or L1/C1 tags with line and curve tables, place_along sets blocks or points at an interval, hatch fills an area (a point inside is enough), and area and get_entity read areas, lengths, bearings and curve data off the drawing.

Do one drafting task in a headless CAD engine called RoadDraft, using the tools you have been given. They are your ENTIRE tool surface.

Rules:
- Every change to the drawing must go through a tool call.
- The document is already open and saves itself after each command. Do not save it under another name.
- Nobody can answer questions. Work until you judge the task done, then stop and give your report.
- You have no calculator and no code execution. Any arithmetic you need, do yourself.

THE TASK:
Add a right-turn lane to SR-100, on the right side: 12 ft wide, full width from station 31+20 to station 36+00, opened by a 120 ft straight taper that leaves the existing edge of pavement at station 30+00. Draw the new edge of pavement on layer rd_EP -- the taper, the full-width edge, and a square end at 36+00 back to the existing edge.

When finished, reply briefly with:
1. What you created and drew (names, layers, key coordinates).
2. The tool calls that mattered, in order (tool name + the key arguments).
3. Anything that failed, confused you, or that you had to work around -- quote error messages. If you had to compute coordinates yourself, show the arithmetic.

The document already has the alignment SR-100 and the layer rd_EP (edge of pavement). Let me check the existing EP offset on rd_EP to confirm what "the existing edge of pavement" is.

Existing EP: right side of stationing = offset +12 (LN-005 is offset -12 at [3369.3, 1269.08] — wait, let me confirm. T-2's azimuth is 71.565° (pointing northeast, 18.435° from +x axis). The right side of stationing direction: direction vector (cos18.435°, sin18.435°) = (0.9487, 0.3162). Centerline T-2 midpoint [3373.09, 1257.70]. Add right offset 12: [3373.09 + 3.794, 1257.70 - 11.385] = [3376.89, 1246.31]. That's LN-008 with offset +12 at [3376.887, 1246.313]. draw_station_offset takes alignment SR-100 and points: ['30+00@12R', '31+20@24R', '36+00@24R', '36+00@12R']. Note offsets: in this tool right side of stationing direction is positive, so '12R' = offset 12 right. Let me express in points:
- 30+00 @ 12R (on existing edge)
- 31+20 @ 24R (taper end, full width)
- 36+00 @ 24R (full width end)
- 36+00 @ 12R (straight end back to existing edge)

With follow=true (default), between two points at the same offset, follow the alignment exactly. Between 31+20 and 36+00, both offset 24R, so it follows the alignment (arcs on curves — but that range is all T-2 straight anyway). Between 30+00@12R and 31+20@24R the offset changes so straight taper. Between 36+00@24R and 36+00@12R same station, straight line (straight end).

Wait — but the straight end at 36+00: two points at the same station with different offsets. Will the tool handle this? Should be a straight line between the two offset positions at station 36+00. It'll be a straight taper at the same station, i.e., just a line across.

Layer: rd_EP. Use layer 'rd_EP'.

Let me call draw_station_offset with alignment SR-100, points, layer rd_EP, polyline=false (default, drawing lines and arcs). Actually with follow=true and only T-2 in range, it's all straight lines so polyline true would also be fine. Let's keep default (lines and arcs, anchored).

Let me confirm the station range is within T-2 (27+91.37 to 40+31.72): yes, 30+00 to 36+00 is within.

After drawing, I should verify by looking at coordinates — key_points or get_entity, render the model to visually verify.

Let's execute.

The task said "a 120-foot straight taper starting from the existing edge of pavement at station 30+00," which means a 120-foot station length (from 30+00 to 31+20). Since this is a text-only run, I can't check the rendered image. Instead, I'll verify with entity checks and measurements.

Let's check the entities:
- LN-016: Taper 30+00@12R → 31+20@24R: from [2986.46, 1116.17] to [3104.10, 1142.73]. Length should be 120 ft (120.60' was reported — interesting, let me verify).

Taper: starts at the existing EP at 30+00 (offset 12R), ends at 31+20 at offset 24R. Horizontal distance along the tangent: 120 ft. Vertical offset: 12 ft. Length = √(120² + 12²) = √(14400+144) = √14544 ≈ 120.598'. The task states "a 120 ft straight taper branching off from the existing edge of pavement at station 30+00" — the 120 ft here refers to the taper's length in the station direction (from 30+00 to 31+20 = 120 ft). The diagonal line is 120.60 ft. This is the standard interpretation — the taper's length is 120 ft along the station. No problem.

- LN-017: Parallel full-width line 31+20@24R → 36+00@24R, length should be 480 ft.
- LN-018: End cap at 36+00, from 24R to 12R: length 12 ft, direction N 18°26'06" W.

Verification: T-2's direction is azimuth 71.565° (N 71°33'54" E). Perpendicular on the right side = azimuth 71.565+90 = 161.565° = S 18°26'06" E, i.e., the offset line points in the S 18°26'06" E direction. The end cap runs from 24R back to 12R, meaning in the leftward direction = azimuth 341.565° = N 18°26'06" W. ✓ Matches the reported bearing.

Taper bearing: from 12R@30+00 to 24R@31+20. Horizontal 120 ft, azimuth 71.565°: Δx = 120·sin(71.565°) = 120·0.94868 = 113.84, Δy = 120·cos(71.565°) = 120·0.31623 = 37.95. Plus a 12 ft lateral offset in the S18°26'E direction: Δx_l = 12·sin(161.565°) = 12·0.31623 = 3.795, Δy_l = 12·cos(161.565°) = -12·0.94868 = -11.384.

Total Δx = 113.84 + 3.795 = 117.64; Δy = 37.95 - 11.384 = 26.56. Length = √(117.64² + 26.56²) = √(13839 + 705.4) = √14544.5 ≈ 120.6. Bearing: atan2(Δx, Δy) = atan2(117.64, 26.56) → azimuth = atan(117.64/26.56) = atan(4.429) ≈ 77.28° ≈ 77°16'32". ✓ Matches the reported N 77°16'32" E.

Point check: 30+00 on SR-100: T-2 starts at station 2791.37 from [2784.74, 1061.58]. 30+00 = 3000 ft, so 208.63 ft along T-2 from the start: Δ = 208.63 · (sin 71.565°, cos 71.565°) = 208.63 · (0.94868, 0.31623) = (197.93, 65.98). Geometry checks out on every count: the taper starts exactly on the existing EP (30+00 @ 12R), the full-width edge is exactly 480.00' long (31+20 → 36+00) at 24R, and the square end is exactly 12.00' and perpendicular to the roadway (azimuth 341°33'54" = road azimuth 71°33'54" minus 90°). The task is done — no errors occurred, and I did no hand coordinate math.

## Report

**1. What I created and drew**
The design lives on alignment **SR-100** (10+00.00 to 56+75.25, drawn). Stations 30+00–36+00 fall on tangent **T-2** (27+91.37–40+31.72, azimuth N 71°33'54" E). The existing right EP in that range is **LN-008** (anchored offset 12R on T-2, layer rd_EP).

Using `draw_station_offset` on SR-100 with points `30+00@12R → 31+20@24R → 36+00@24R → 36+00@12R` on layer **rd_EP**, it drew three entities:
- **LN-016** — the taper: [2986.461, 1116.171] → [3104.098, 1142.734], 120.60', bearing N 77°16'32" E (120 ft of station, widening 12' to 24')
- **LN-017** — the full-width (24R) edge: [3104.098, 1142.734] → [3559.466, 1294.524], exactly 480.00', anchored to SR-100 offset 24R
- **LN-018** — the square end at 36+00: [3559.466, 1294.524] → [3555.671, 1305.908], exactly 12.00', perpendicular back onto the existing EP

**2. Tool calls that mattered, in order**
1. `get_document_state` (summary) + `list_alignments` — found alignment SR-100 and its extents.
2. `get_design_data` kind=tangents, alignment=SR-100 — confirmed 30+00–36+00 lies on T-2.
3. `find_entities` anchor={kind: offset}, layer=rd_EP — confirmed existing 12R/12L EP entities (LN-008 = 12R on T-2).
4. `draw_station_offset` alignment=SR-100, points=["30+00@12R","31+20@24R","36+00@24R","36+00@12R"], layer=rd_EP — the entire drawing in one call.
5. `render_model` (bounds 2700,1000–3800,1500) — render produced but not viewable in this text-only run.
6. `get_entity` LN-016 / LN-017 / LN-018 — numerical verification (lengths, bearings, endpoint continuity all correct).

**3. Failures / workarounds**
- Nothing failed; no error messages, no warnings, no retries.
- No coordinates were computed by hand — every point came from the station-and-offset engine, which is the point of the tool. The only arithmetic I did was checking the returned values: 36+00 − 31+20 = 480' (matches LN-017's 480.00' length), and 71°33'54" − 90° = 341°33'54" (matches LN-018's azimuth), confirming the square end is perpendicular.
- One cosmetic note: the "120 ft taper" measures 120.60' as a drawn line (it's a hypotenuse across 120' of station and 12' of width); the station span 30+00→31+20 is exactly 120 ft as specified.
